findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the `--until` duration format and the expiry semantics (auto-resume trigger and who enforces it), and add a covering acceptance criterion.
evidence: Plan says 'offer an optional --until <duration> (Argo Rollouts ships both shapes)' but never states the accepted duration syntax nor the auto-resume mechanism when it expires.
No AC references --until at all.
findings.finding: The optional `--until <duration>` flag has no specified duration format/units and no defined expiry behavior (does the bridge auto-resume when the duration elapses, and who/what triggers that?). An executor cannot implement it without choosing these.
scenarios: Executor must guess between ISO-8601 durations, Go-style '30m', or seconds; and must decide whether expiry is enforced by the reconciler on next pass or a separate job.
findings.suggested_fix: State: `--until` accepts a Go-style duration (e.g. `30m`, `2h`); on the first pass after `paused_at + until`, the reconciler treats the gate as expired and proceeds, logging an auto-resume.

findings.checklist_item: Name `.github/workflows/reconcile-bridge.yml` and its exit-code `case` block (add an exit-4 `::notice` arm) as the concrete edit target for the 'workflow treats a paused bridge as a notice' AC.
evidence: .github/workflows/reconcile-bridge.yml:265-270 has a `case "$rc" in` with explicit arms for 0/75/3 and a catch-all `*)  echo "::error::Reconcile failed (exit $rc)"; exit "$rc"` — exit 4 currently falls into the error branch and fails the job
The plan's body references '__main__.py:613' returning exit 4 but never names reconcile-bridge.yml as an edit target; only the AC gestures generically at 'the workflow'
findings.finding: The final AC requires the CI workflow to treat a paused bridge (exit 4) as a notice, but the plan body never names the workflow file or the specific exit-code branch that must change.
findings.location: AC: 'The workflow treats a paused bridge as a notice, not an error'
scenarios: Author implements pause/resume + clean exit 4 but leaves the workflow untouched; every scheduled run of a paused bridge fails the job (red) instead of emitting a ::notice
findings.suggested_fix: In reconcile-bridge.yml's `case "$rc" in`, add `4)  echo "::notice::Reconcile bridge is paused (exit 4) — skipping." ;;` before the `*)` catch-all so exit 4 does not fail the job.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify who enforces `--until` expiry (lazy reader-side re-interpretation vs. active clear) and how expiry interacts with an old binary that has no expiry logic, so an expired pause cannot leave old-binary passes wedged.
evidence: Plan: 'offer an optional --until <duration> (Argo Rollouts ships both shapes)'
No AC or mechanism text names the expiry enforcer; ACs cover blob shape, write path, decoder test, Mode-member guard, exit-4, no-remote, and workflow-notice, but none covers expiry
_decode_gate (_ref_lock.py:658-671) has no time/expiry awareness, so an old binary cannot honour --until
findings.finding: The plan adopts an optional `--until <duration>` bound on pause but never specifies WHICH component enforces expiry or where the un-pause decision lives (lazy reader-side check vs. an active clear). This is a load-bearing mechanism decision because expiry logic has no counterpart in an OLD binary: a lazy reader-side interpretation of `paused_at + until` un-pauses new binaries at expiry while old binaries stay wedged on the still-present `gated_mode: reconcile-check` blob, silently diverging fleet behaviour the epic is trying to keep uniform.
findings.location: Design spike findings — final bullet ('offer an optional --until <duration>')
scenarios: An operator sets pause --until 30m; 30m later a new-binary pass resumes but an old-binary pass on another host still reads the gate and stays wedged
The ref persists on origin after expiry with no writer to clear it

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Correct the 'everything is blocked' claim to note reconcile-check itself (target==gated) is NOT blocked, and confirm that a read-only reconcile-check pass running while paused is acceptable (or choose a compat value that blocks it too).
evidence: mode.py:21-27: reconcile-check is _ORDERED[0]; _advisory_lock.py:250 returns `target_mode > gated_mode`
For target_mode=RECONCILE_CHECK the comparison is False (equal, not strictly greater), so the pass is NOT blocked
Plan claims 'everything reaching the check is blocked'
findings.finding: The plan asserts absolutely that with the compatibility value 'everything reaching the check is blocked', but the mechanism does not block a read-only reconcile-check pass on an old binary: check_phase_gate blocks only when target_mode > gated_mode, and RECONCILE_CHECK > RECONCILE_CHECK is False. A reconcile-check pass therefore runs to completion (exit 0) on an old binary while the bridge is 'paused'.
findings.location: Design spike findings — first bullet ('reconcile-check is the bottom rung, so everything reaching the check is blocked')
scenarios: An old-binary reconcile-check pass fires while paused and exits 0, reporting GREEN

evidence: Plan: 'offer an optional --until <duration> (Argo Rollouts ships both shapes)'

Codebase: the only '--until' is the metrics date-range flag (src/rebar/_commands/metrics.py:126), unrelated in type/semantics; no duration parser exists in the rebar_reconciler package (search for '--until' under that dir returned no matches)

ABSENCE: plan does not specify who/what re-evaluates expiry, at which read, or the time source — an auto-un-pause is a fail-open risk the plan otherwise takes pains to avoid (the gated_mode fail-open discussion)
findings.finding: The optional `--until <duration>` flag is introduced by OSS-mimicry ("Argo Rollouts ships both shapes") but serves no Acceptance Criterion — none of the seven ACs exercise expiry, auto-resume, or duration bounds, and no existing duration-parse precedent in the reconciler package is cited. It reads as YAGNI/resume-driven scope rather than a current done-definition, and it silently introduces an unspecified auto-un-pause/time-source concern.
findings.location: Design spike findings, final bullet: '--until <duration>'; Acceptance Criteria (7 items)
scenarios: Author ships --until, but no test covers auto-resume, leaving an untested un-pause path
A --until value silently expires and un-pauses the fleet-wide gate with no operator action, contradicting the 'refuse loudly' / notice-not-error posture

evidence: 'Alertmanager makes the comment mandatory and rejects zero-duration silences' — an intended validation with no asserted test

optional '--until <duration>' introduced with no boundary test for zero/invalid duration
findings.finding: The plan specifies tests for the compat/wedge/fail-open/exit-4/no-remote paths but names no failure-path test for the new pause/resume CLI behaviors it introduces — required-reason rejection, resume-when-not-paused, and the --until zero/invalid-duration rejection that the plan itself says Alertmanager enforces.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria (pause/resume, --until) and Design spike findings
scenarios: Operator runs pause with an empty reason and it silently succeeds
Operator passes --until 0 and the gate is created with no bound
resume issued when not paused behaves unexpectedly

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify pause-when-already-paused, resume-when-not-paused, and empty-reason rejection behavior for the CLI verbs.
evidence: Plan requires a reason and cites Alertmanager rejecting zero-duration silences, but does not state what pause does when a gate already exists, or resume when none exists.
AC set covers no-remote (AC6) but not idempotent/absent-state cases.
findings.finding: The pause/resume CLI surface omits non-happy-path states: pausing an already-paused bridge, resuming a bridge that is not paused, and empty/whitespace reason handling are not specified even though the OSS-validation note stresses a mandatory reason.
scenarios: Operator runs `resume` on a bridge that was never paused and gets an unclear error or silent success; operator re-runs `pause` and overwrites the original reason/paused_at, losing audit provenance.
findings.suggested_fix: Define: `pause` on an existing gate reports the current pause (or requires `--force` to overwrite); `resume` on an un-paused bridge exits cleanly with a notice; a blank reason is rejected loudly.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Define concurrency handling for pause/resume ref writes (e.g. compare-and-swap on the expected old ref oid, and behavior on a rejected non-fast-forward update).
evidence: Plan: gate is 'a remote-persisted git ref' 'shared on origin'.
No mention of ref-update compare-and-swap, expected-old-oid, or last-writer-wins handling for concurrent pause/resume.
findings.finding: The gate blob is a shared git ref on `origin` that pause/resume now mutate, but the plan does not address concurrent writers: two operators (or an operator racing an --until expiry) doing pause/resume against the same ref is a check-then-act on shared state with no atomicity/CAS mechanism named.
findings.location: AC2 'pause "<reason>" and resume are the only supported write path'
scenarios: Operator A resumes while Operator B pauses against origin simultaneously — one non-fast-forward push silently loses, leaving the bridge in the opposite of the intended state with no error surfaced.
findings.suggested_fix: Require pause/resume to push with an expected-old-oid CAS and, on rejection, re-read and report the conflicting state rather than clobbering it.
